line_items.reasoning: Citigroup reaffirmed its full-year 2024 revenue guidance of $80B–$81B; Q1 showed strong Services (+8%), IB (+35%), and USPB (+10%) wins, but Markets revenues fell 7% YoY and card fee headwinds from the late-fee rule were acknowledged as embedded in the existing guidance range, leaving the full-year target intact but not clearly exceeded.

NII ex-markets was guided to be down only modestly, but Wealth NII dropped 13% YoY from lower deposit spreads, USPB credit costs surged 34% YoY with the Retail Services NCL rate exceeding the high end of full-year guidance and expected to remain above range in Q2, pointing to worse-than-guided margin pressure.

The medium-term RoTCE target of 11%–12% by 2026 was reaffirmed and CET1 improved to 13.5%, but near-term RoTCE remains pressured (Wealth at only 4.6%), and no explicit EPS beat vs. guidance was reported, keeping this inline with the reaffirmed medium-term trajectory.

The organizational simplification was completed ahead of schedule with ~7,000 positions eliminated and $1.5B in annualized run-rate saves already locked in, tracking well ahead of the $700M–$1B of elevated severance/simplification costs embedded in the $53.5B–$53.8B expense guidance, suggesting expenses are trending favorably.

The medium-term $2.0B–$2.5B net run-rate savings target was reaffirmed and the organizational simplification was declared complete in Q1-2024, with $1.5B in annualized saves already achieved—ahead of the pace implied by the prior guidance for a multi-year headcount reduction program.
